title: Saying Goodbye
goal: End an encounter, acknowledge the time together, and make clear whether future contact is a plan or a general wish.

runs.text: An ending can begin before the final
Bye
. These expressions let the other person know the interaction is coming to a close:
I need to get going.
You need to leave.
I'm going to head out.
You are about to leave.
I have to go.
A clear statement that you need to stop.
I need to end the call now.
Explicitly close a call.
After visiting a friend

blocks.caption: Signal that you are leaving · Jamie & Sky

runs.text: It was great to see you
acknowledges the encounter.
Take care
gives a friendly closing wish. You can answer
You too
when the same wish applies to both people.

rows.text: A closing anticipating later contact, without necessarily fixing a time.
Refer to an understood Tuesday meeting.
Wish someone a pleasant evening as you leave.
Close contact at night or before sleep.

runs.text: Good evening
can open an evening encounter;
Good night
generally has a different job. Chapter 1 introduced that contrast.
At a meeting with a new contact,
It was a pleasure meeting you
is an available choice. A shorter
Nice meeting you
can do similar work.
Thank you for your time
is useful after someone has made time to help or meet you. Professional contact does not require every one of these phrases.
A project conversation ends

turns.speaker: Sky

runs.text: That answers my questions. Thank you for your time.

turns.en: That answers my questions. Thank you for your time.

turns.speaker: Jamie

runs.text: You're welcome. I'll send the document this afternoon.

turns.en: You're welcome. I'll send the document this afternoon.

runs.text: Great. Good talking with you.
You too. Goodbye.
The document promise belongs to this scene. The closing itself does not require a promise.

study.title: Future contact can be specific or open

runs.text: We should do this again sometime
expresses interest in another meeting, but it is not a scheduled appointment.
See you Friday at six
refers to a more specific arrangement.

turns.speaker: Jamie

runs.text: This was fun. Let's do it again.

turns.en: This was fun. Let's do it again.

turns.speaker: Sky

runs.text: I'd like that. I'll text you next week.

turns.en: I'd like that. I'll text you next week.

runs.text: Sounds good. Bye.

blocks.caption: Future contact can be specific or open · Jamie & Sky

runs.text: Here Sky offers a next step. If you want a definite time,
When are you free?
can begin scheduling in Chapter 12. If you do not want to promise future contact, you can simply close with
It was good talking with you. Take care
Have a safe trip
wishes someone well when they are traveling. If you are not traveling too,
Thanks
may fit better than automatically saying
You too
Catch you later
and
See ya
can close a familiar exchange.
I gotta go
is an informal written representation of
I've got to go
I'm out
can announce your departure in a casual scene. Choose the style you intend; none is a required way to sound American.

practice.title: Bring the encounter to an end

runs.text: On your own, speak both people's lines. Try a supported ending first, then hide the models and change the relationship.
End a visit to a friend's home. Include a departure signal, one acknowledgment, and a goodbye. Let the friend respond.
End a brief work call after getting an answer. You do not need to promise another meeting. Support:
That answers my question
Thanks for your help
Good talking with you
A friend says
We should get lunch again sometime
. You would like to, but no date is fixed. Reply without pretending there is already an appointment.
You have agreed to meet Friday at six. Close with that plan clear. Your partner answers
See you then
Someone wishes you
Have a safe trip
. They are staying home. Give a reply that fits.
Optional: you are leaving a casual game night. Try
I gotta go. Catch you later
, then give the friend's response.
Sample possibilities
I need to get going. Thanks for having me. — You're welcome. Take care. — You too. Bye.
That answers my question. Thanks for your help. — Happy to help. — Good talking with you. Goodbye.
I'd like that. Let's find a day next week.
See you Friday at six. — See you then.
Thanks. Take care.
I gotta go. Catch you later. — Okay. See ya.
Check:
Could the other person tell you were ending the exchange? Was future contact confirmed or still open? Did your reply fit the wish or information actually given?
